statement: Ella has three 5-cent coins. How much money does she have?

choices.misconception: I added the 3 and the 5 instead of counting three coins.
I counted only two of the three coins.
I counted four coins instead of three.
I wrote the two numbers next to each other instead of adding the coins.

hints: Count on in fives, once for each coin.
Each coin is worth five, so count five, then ten, and keep going until you have counted one number for each coin you have. Then stop.
5, then 10, then 15, one count for each of the three coins.

solutions.reliable: Counting in fives for three coins gives 5, 10, 15 cents. The idea to keep: when every coin is worth the same, count on by that amount and make one count for each coin.

whyOnTest: Adding the number of coins to the value of a coin is the standard mix-up, and it is the first choice here.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
